The Chirps and the Welcome Tree

The Great Acorn Almost-Race

Chip wanted to bring the fastest game in the garden to Everybody Day. He lined up three acorns at the top of a plank. Down at the bottom Bella held a leaf for a finish flag.

“Ready, steady, ROLL!” The long acorn shot straight down. The fat acorn wobbled. The third one rolled in a circle and came to rest against Chip’s foot. He named it Pancake.

They raced again. The long acorn won. They raced backward. The long acorn won. Toad shut his eyes and picked a racer at random. It was the long acorn. Nobody cheered very much.

Chip sulked on the starting line. Bella quietly took Pancake to the side of the plank. She laid down two bent twigs with a winding space between them. “Can yours do this?” she asked.

Pancake went round the first bend like a duck on a pond. It went round the second and stopped neatly between two daisies. The long acorn shot out of the lane and into a sock someone had hung to dry.

Chip laughed until his zigzag nearly wrinkled. “You found its game!” he said. Toad wanted a game for the wobbler. They gave it three soft moss bumps to bounce over. It bounced over two and sat on the third.

Soon the hill held a fast lane, a bendy lane and a bouncing lane. Racers could pick a race to fit their acorn. Chip picked the bendy one. He particularly wanted a turn with Pancake.

For the Welcome Tree he drew an acorn on a crooked track. He left the finish flag off. Somebody had found a fourth game. Bella was teaching the flag how to wobble, too.

Read together

How many different kinds of races could one small hill hold?
